@graph.name: Cup and Tub Case Packer
@graph.description: A cup and tub case packer is a top-load machine that picks filled, lidded cups and tubs from the line and places them upright into shipping cases in a set pack pattern. TRF Industrial Automation packs cups and tubs with TRFRapidpack and cups with TRFOnepack. The right one is defined mainly by your line setup and speed, not by the container alone.

mainEntity.name: Does a Cup and Tub Case Packer Need a Vision System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when product position varies. When containers arrive in controlled lanes from the sealer, indexed picking is enough. When the flow is variable or several SKUs share the infeed, TRFRapidpack can pack with vision-guided delta robots that locate each container before the pick. The choice depends on your infeed and on how many formats the machine runs.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Integrated Case Packer and Separate Erecting, Packing and Sealing Machines?

acceptedAnswer.text: An integrated case packer erects the case, loads it and seals it in one coordinated machine, with one controls platform. Separate machines each need their own interfaces, controls and floor space. TRFOnepack is the integrated option, for applications of about 20 to 50 products per minute, and it can start standalone and later join a complete TRF end-of-line system.

mainEntity.name: What Floor Space Does an Integrated Case Packing Machine Require?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the case size, the pack pattern, the infeed and how operators reach the machine. What changes the answer most is consolidation: TRFOnepack combines case erecting, robotic packing and case sealing in one machine architecture, which takes less floor space than three machines in series. TRF places the machine in your floor plan, with infeed and discharge, during the application review.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFRapidpack is designed for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the container, the pick tool, the pack pattern and how cups and tubs leave the sealer, and TRF engineering validates it for each line before the design is closed.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. The signals and buffers between your filler and the case packer, and the handoff to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: packers per shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, cases the line can ship once manual packing stops limiting it, damaged lids and dropped containers avoided, and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
